pr.title: Fix iOS pod installation without Google OAuth setup
pr.body:
## Summary

The iOS release build fails during CocoaPods installation when optional Google OAuth settings are absent. The native Google Sign-In dependency still autolinks, but its configuration plugin—and required AppCheck dependency module maps—are omitted.

Add a targeted Expo build-properties fallback for GoogleUtilities and RecaptchaInterop while preserving configured Google sign-in. Include an isolated, manual macOS pod diagnostic in the existing workflow; it excludes every release job and does not build or sign an app.

Closes #48. Original failure: [release run 37874954697](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37874954697), [iOS build adde78c5](https://expo.dev/accounts/matthewchartier/projects/little-say/builds/adde78c5-19e6-40d5-8e58-d3b89abf6d46).

## Test plan and behavior evidence

- **Missing OAuth settings, real macOS:** [diagnostic run 37881372074](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37881372074) reproduced the exact AppCheckCore module-map error on baseline `b46e9e8` (`pod install` exit 1). Source `06b4b00` completed prebuild and `pod install` (exit 0; 116 pods), with the same relevant pod versions.
- **Diagnostic limitation:** that workflow concluded **failure** because its version parser selected nested dependency constraints from the successful lockfile. The parser is corrected at final head `d88515b`; its new regression fails before the correction and passes afterward. Local replay of the retained lockfile agrees with independent YAML parsing. No hosted rerun occurred. Application configuration is unchanged from the macOS-tested source.
- **Configured sign-in and Android:** the existing Nitro pod directives remain unchanged; all 44 baseline/final Android prebuild files are byte-identical. The maintained configuration regression fails on the original missing-scheme case and passes with the fix.
- **Local checks:** 34 focused release/configuration/diagnostic/isolation tests and script typechecking pass. Release metadata and application/server/core typechecks passed. [Final-head CI passed](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37881717383), including repository checks/builds, service integration and account-browser tests.

This is a non-UI build-configuration change. [Original generated evidence](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/tree/92f219f4fd3bcac29a935726cfb2b74ce699663d) and [raw macOS results, versions, hashes and parser replay](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/73a48868d6df246f4f9b8951dfa4dd8542afe16c/macos-run-37881372074.md) are retained outside product history. The raw failed diagnostic results are preserved unchanged.

## Supporting checks and limitations

The macOS check used Xcode 26.4.1 and CocoaPods 1.16.2; all seven non-diagnostic jobs skipped. Successful pod installation is not native compilation or signed-build validation. No archive, EAS build, release retry, store submission or deployment occurred. The [independent technical and evidence assessment](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/49#issuecomment-6074115939) verified the scoped fix, retained native evidence and published scope.

issue.title: iOS pods fail without optional Google OAuth configuration
issue.body:
## Problem

The iOS [Cut release run 37874954697](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37874954697) failed during CocoaPods installation: AppCheckCore’s Swift integration requires module maps for GoogleUtilities and RecaptchaInterop. [EAS build adde78c5-19e6-40d5-8e58-d3b89abf6d46](https://expo.dev/accounts/matthewchartier/projects/little-say/builds/adde78c5-19e6-40d5-8e58-d3b89abf6d46) used source b46e9e83ffacb2e3846486fb7a64a57d1203f372. The native dependency autolinks even when the optional Google OAuth scheme is absent, but its configuration plugin is then omitted.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Supply the missing scoped module-map configuration without changing authentication/account access, unrelated dependencies or framework linkage.
- Preserve the existing configured Google sign-in path and Android generated behavior.
- Maintain a focused regression covering absent and configured OAuth settings.
- Provide a manual-only macOS check of actual iOS prebuild and CocoaPods installation, recording exact source/tool/dependency identities and distinguishing baseline reproduction from final success.
- Keep this separate from signed builds, EAS/release retries, submissions, deployment and readiness changes.

## Implementation plan

Use the Expo SDK 57 supported per-pod build-properties fallback only when Nitro’s existing configuration plugin is absent. Preserve baseline/final generated configuration evidence. Add an isolated manual diagnostic mode to the existing dispatchable workflow, with read-only permissions, no persisted checkout credentials or release secrets, and all release jobs explicitly excluded. Independent safety review must inspect the published mode before dispatch.

The user authorized local preparation, then explicitly approved draft publication and one bounded macOS CocoaPods check on 2026-10-09. No signed build or release retry is authorized.

## Implementing Codex task

01a11eae-26c8-75b2-8a04-c06eece7701d

## Implementing PR

[Draft PR #49 — Fix iOS pod installation without Google OAuth setup](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/49).

+  ios-pods:
+    if: inputs.ios_pods_only

+          [[ "$BASELINE_SHA" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]

+      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262

+      - name: Validate fix without Google OAuth configuration
+        id: fix

+      - name: Retain exact inputs, generated pod files and diagnostics

+        env:

@@ -6,6 +6,10 @@ To validate a proposed change before merging, select its branch and enable **val
 
 The same source-only boundary can run locally as `npm run release:validate` after `npm ci`, with an isolated PostgreSQL test database and the explicit `TEST_PG*` settings described in [testing](testing.md). It requires no release command or production Firebase project. Existing PR CI coverage is unchanged; validation-only runs are manual.
 
+For the iOS AppCheck module-map diagnostic, enable **both `validation_only` and `ios_pods_only`** on the reviewed branch. Supply its full reviewed SHA as `ios_pods_head` and the failing source SHA as `ios_pods_baseline`. A mismatched head or missing validation flag fails before checkout; either validation flag excludes every release job. Only the macOS pod job runs, using isolated credential-free checkouts, Node 24.19.0, Ruby 3.3.12, CocoaPods 1.16.2 and Xcode 26.4.1. It clears optional Google OAuth configuration and disables dotenv loading, then runs locked dependency installation, iOS prebuild and `pod install`. It does not compile, sign, submit or invoke EAS.
+
+The diagnostic requires the baseline's specific AppCheckCore module-map failure and a passing fix, at GoogleSignIn 10.0.0 / AppCheckCore 11.3.2 / GoogleUtilities 8.1.4 / RecaptchaInterop 101.0.0. Different failures or dependency drift fail visibly rather than certifying the comparison. The `ios-pods-<source>-<attempt>` artifact retains source/tool identities, hashed logs, generated pod configuration and the successful Podfile.lock for 30 days; preserve needed evidence separately before expiry. This manual check is not an automatic PR gate or signed-build validation.
+

 | --- | --- | --- |
 | Build mode | `auto`, `force_all` | `auto` |
